title: Planner: private tasks stored in your private plan instead of Microsoft To Do
summary: The storage change, automatic rollout, dates and Planner licensing are supported. The page nevertheless presents audit coverage as an open question despite Microsoft documenting support across plan types and containers, and labels Teams app automation undocumented despite an existing PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: The Planner app can be blocked tenant-wide at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block.
claims.quote:
In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps.
To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: The Teams admin centre control governs the Planner app in Teams, not the private-task storage destination.
claims.quote: You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Automation for changing whether the Planner app is available in Microsoft Teams is not yet documented.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app.
-IsBlocked
The state of the app in the tenant.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind 'powershell', call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean>', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp'. Retain the warning that the examples inconsistently describe the Boolean values; do not prescribe $true as a verified blocking value.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference labels its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking an app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app

claims.claim: Whether Purview audit applies to new private tasks in a private plan remains undocumented.
claims.quote:
Purview's integrated audit logs are supported across plan types and containers.

Retention policy isn't currently supported.

Purview integration depends on an appropriate license for Purview (like the E5 license).
claims.fix: Remove the first Open questions bullet beginning 'Is Purview audit applied to new private tasks'. The cited Planner security page already states that integrated audit logs are supported across plan types and containers.

claims.where: Open questions: first bullet, 'as it is to private tasks in Exchange today'
claims.claim: Existing To Do private-task activities can be audited in Purview.
claims.quote: To audit events for Microsoft To Do activities, you need a paid Project Plan 1 license (or higher) in addition to the relevant Microsoft 365 license that includes entitlements to Audit (Standard).
claims.fix: Remove the clause 'as it is to private tasks in Exchange today' with the first Open questions bullet. This comparison relies on an uncited audit reference and omits that reference's additional licensing qualification.
